title: SLO-driven fanout bailout controller for stream-stable active-active failover
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a controller that reduces cross-region fanout (bailout) in a graduated manner when SLOs degrade in a region while preserving streaming session continuity. The controller must coordinate: (1) SLO evaluation and hysteresis windows, (2) a phased traffic-shearing plan (not all-or-nothing cutover), (3) circuit breaker escalation for downstream overloaded nodes, (4) KV prefix checkpointing and stitch tokens to permit session resumption on a secondary region, and (5) safe autoscale/capacity hints to Dedicated. Goal: keep hosted API availability above 99.95% and bound P95 token latency degradation to <2x during region partial failures for streaming and long-lived sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Controller evaluates region SLOs (latency p95, error rate, queue depth) and triggers phased bailout when thresholds crossed
Phased bailout reduces fanout incrementally (5%, 15%, 50%, 95%) with configurable hold windows and can be aborted/rolled back
Streaming sessions are preserved: KV prefix checkpointing is performed before final diversion and stitch token issued to client-side proxy
Circuit breaker layer short-circuits unhealthy backend pools and marks capacities in telemetry within 30s of crossing threshold
Demo load test: simulated 30% region node degradation results in <5% increase in session reconnects and P95 latency stays within spec
Fallback policy: if secondary region capacity insufficient, controller applies load-shedding policies by priority tier and returns explicit Retry-After semantics
tasks: Design SLO evaluation rules and hysteresis (SRE + product input)
Implement bailout controller service with phase gates and trial rollbacks
Extend gateway to accept stitch tokens and KV prefix pointers during handoff
Add circuit breaker escalation hooks to serving runtime with 3 severity levels
Create e2e test harness for multi-region degradation scenarios
Dashboard: SLO triggers, bailout phases, session stitch counts, and shed volumes
Run staged canary in 2 regions with traffic replay tests
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Chosen phased fanout reduction rather than immediate cutover to avoid mass session churn (DECISION by SRE & Runtime)
2026-03-11: Use stitch tokens + KV prefix checkpointing vs state replication because of bandwidth and consistency trade-offs
2026-03-11: Circuit breaker thresholds set to p95 latency > 1.8x baseline OR error_rate > 5% OR queue_depth > 300ms-equivalent
2026-03-12: Bailout phases chosen: 5% (probe), 15% (soft-shift), 50% (major), 95% (drain) with default hold windows [30s, 90s, 5m, 10m]
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag rollout to 10% of gateways in us-west and eu-central behind a runtime flag
Phase 1: Canary exercises with synthetic stream sessions (low risk) for 48h
Phase 2: Expand to 50% gateways and enable KV checkpointing across regions
Phase 3: Full regional rollout and enable automatic bailout controller for P0 incidents
Rollback: global flag off; controller will reverse phased shifts and expire stitch tokens after 15m
telemetry_requirements: Emit region SLO measurements every 10s (p50/p95/p99 latency, 1m error rate, queue depth)
Emit bailout decisions and phase transitions with reason codes and sampled trace ids
Track stitch-token issuance, successful resumes, and failed resume attempts per 5m window
Expose circuit breaker state per backend pool (closed, open, half-open) and last trip reason
Add cost metrics for cross-region KV checkpoint bytes transferred
risks: Cross-region KV transfer increases egress costs and may hit customer data residency constraints
Stitch token misuse could allow session takeover if not tied to connection fingerprints (mitigate with short TTL and HMAC)
If secondary region is underprovisioned, phased bailout still may cause user-visible latency spikes
Complexity of controller increases operational surface area and possible oscillation between phases (mitigate via conservative hysteresis)
review_feedback: PM (Miguel Rivera): prioritize explicit Retry-After semantics for non-recoverable shed decisions
Design (Elena Rossi): client UX needs clear reconnect guidance; add SDK helpers to handle stitch tokens
Security (Priya Nair): require HMAC binding of stitch tokens to connection metadata and short TTL
SRE (Daniel Kim): recommend 2-minute cold-start hold for autoscale to avoid flip-flopping during brief blips
